title: Tame fixed subschemes form a weakly boundary normal crossings family
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian regular separated scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $B$ be a strict normal crossings divisor [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], and let a finite group $G$ act on $X$, preserving $B$, tamely and generically freely. Tame means that each geometric stabilizer has order invertible in the residue field; generically free means free on a dense invariant open. Suppose $B$ is $G$-strict: distinct translates of a component are disjoint. For each nontrivial subgroup $H\leq G$ let $X^H$ be the closed subscheme equalizing all $h:X\to X$ with the identity, with empty fixed subschemes omitted. Then $X^H$ is regular and nowhere dense and has normal crossings with $B$. Scheme-theoretically $X^H\cap X^K=X^{\langle H,K\rangle}$, so the same assertions hold for every nonempty intersection. At a geometric point fixed by $H$, its tangent space is the $H$-invariant subspace of the tangent space of $X$. The union of the supports of these fixed subschemes is precisely the complement of the largest free open. They are permuted by $G$ via $gX^H=X^{gHg^{-1}}$.
